title: Plugin SDK manifest (WordPress)
description: Declarative manifest for a WordPress plugin built with Plugin SDK. Describes settings pages, REST routes, and database tables. The PHP runtime (plugin-sdk/wp) reads this file at boot, validates against this schema, and registers the corresponding WP hooks with capability checks, nonce verification, and JSON-schema validation built in.

$schema.description: Editor-tooling schema reference. Ignored by the runtime.

platform.description: Target platform. WordPress is the only supported value today.

name.description: Human-readable plugin name. Appears in the WP plugins list.

slug.description: Kebab-case identifier used for menu slugs, asset handles, and the main PHP file name.

textDomain.description: WP i18n text domain. Usually equals slug.

version.description: Semver. Used to drive db-version comparisons + asset cache busting.

namespace.description: PHP PSR-4 root namespace for the plugin (e.g. "Acme\\Forms").

settings.description: Optional admin settings page. Renders under Settings or Tools (or as a top-level menu).

rest.description: Optional REST API surface. Routes are registered on rest_api_init with cap checks and JSON-schema body validation.

database.description: Optional custom tables. Migration runs on activate or version bump.

routes.description: Optional virtual routes — URL patterns the plugin serves itself (llms.txt, a .md rendition, a manifest). The runtime registers the rewrite rule, whitelists the query var, intercepts at parse_request priority 0, self-heals rewrites after updates, and primes + flushes rules on activation.

uninstall.description: Optional uninstall declaration. The scaffolded uninstall.php reads this fragment directly (no SDK boot) and removes the listed options — and the plugin's database tables when dropTables is true.

options.description: Option names to delete on uninstall.

dropTables.description: Drop the tables declared under database.tables.

slug.description: Menu slug. Defaults to the plugin slug if omitted.

attach.description: Attach the fields to a CORE settings screen instead of creating a page. Fields in a section with id 'default' render inside the core screen's own table (e.g. right under Search engine visibility on 'reading'); other sections render below it. When set, parent/menuTitle/menuIcon are ignored and no menu item is added — the right choice for small plugins that would otherwise add a whole page for two checkboxes.

parent.description: Where the page lives in the WP admin menu. 'top-level' creates a top-level menu item. Ignored when attach is set.

menuIcon.description: Dashicon name (e.g. 'dashicons-admin-generic') or a data: URL. Only used when parent='top-level'.

optionGroup.description: Settings group name passed to register_setting(). Defaults to <slug>_settings.

description.description: Help text shown below the field.

showIf.description: Conditional visibility: the field's row is shown only while a sibling field (same section option) has the given value. Checkbox controllers compare against true/false; everything else compares string values.

rows.description: For type='keyedSelect' only: static row map of key → row label. Rows already present in the stored value render too, so dynamic keys (added by code via the option) survive.

default.description: Default value. Type must match the field type.

options.description: For type='select' and type='keyedSelect'. Each option is either a string or { value, label }.

path.description: Path under the REST namespace, leading slash. Supports WP path patterns like '/(?P<id>\d+)'.

capability.description: Required cap. If omitted, the route is public (rare — usually a mistake).

schema.description: JSON Schema for the request body (POST/PUT/PATCH). The runtime validates incoming JSON against this before invoking the handler.

name.description: Table name without the WP table prefix. Final name = $wpdb->prefix + slug-prefix + name.

type.description: SQL column type. Examples: BIGINT UNSIGNED, VARCHAR(255), TEXT, DATETIME, TINYINT(1).

default.description: SQL default. Use the literal string 'CURRENT_TIMESTAMP' for timestamps.
